svg.title: First-County Lien Entry Workflow
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-county-lien-entry-workflow; chapter number: 1; title: First-County Lien Entry Workflow; subtitle: From a phone call to the county to a logged certificate; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Call the County; value: Step 1; detail: Ask how many liens sold last year and how many people attended; 200 to 500 liens with 20 bidders beats 30 liens with 50.; step: 02; label: Learn the State Ceiling; value: Step 2; detail: Statutory ceilings cited include Florida 18%, Arizona 16%, Iowa 24% and Illinois 36%.; step: 03; label: Look at the Parcel and Set an Exit; value: Step 3; detail: No bid on any parcel you have not looked at and have no exit strategy for; never bid on a lien you would not be comfortable owning.; step: 04; label: Bid Above Zero in Florida; value: Step 4; detail: A $1,000 lien bid at 0.25% and redeemed in 3 months pays the 5% floor of $50; a 0% bid gets no minimum at all.; step: 05; label: Log Dates and Reserve Legal Fees; value: Step 5; detail: Record redemption and expiration dates the day you buy (Florida certificates expire without a deed application within seven years) and reserve roughly $2,000 to $5,000 per file for attorney and foreclosure fees.; caption: Start small in one county: size the competition, know the rate ceiling, look before bidding, respect the Florida floor, and calendar every deadline.; assumptions note: Rates and redemption floors are state-specific practitioner claims; the five-step order is an organizing sequence built from their separate tips.; note: Sources: Dustin Hahn (eNKIUQC6io0 @ 00:05:44); Ted Thomas via Gerald Harris (nMj50Itu21Q @ 00:03:13); Ted Thomas (JcAwqIfK0vo @ 00:12:26); Lien Ledger (H9fPhqUYPfc @ 00:04:40, 00:05:50, 00:08:00); Tax Sale Secrets (fIPCLCdZlAU @ 00:08:59).

rect.title: step: 01; label: Call the County; value: Step 1; detail: Ask how many liens sold last year and how many people attended; 200 to 500 liens with 20 bidders beats 30 liens with 50.

text.title: Ask how many liens sold last year and how many people attended; 200 to 500 liens with 20 bidders beats 30 liens with 50.

rect.title: step: 02; label: Learn the State Ceiling; value: Step 2; detail: Statutory ceilings cited include Florida 18%, Arizona 16%, Iowa 24% and Illinois 36%.

text.title: Statutory ceilings cited include Florida 18%, Arizona 16%, Iowa 24% and Illinois 36%.

rect.title: step: 03; label: Look at the Parcel and Set an Exit; value: Step 3; detail: No bid on any parcel you have not looked at and have no exit strategy for; never bid on a lien you would not be comfortable owning.

text.title: Look at the Parcel and Set an Exit
No bid on any parcel you have not looked at and have no exit strategy for; never bid on a lien you would not be comfortable owning.
text.tspan: No bid on any parcel you…

rect.title: step: 04; label: Bid Above Zero in Florida; value: Step 4; detail: A $1,000 lien bid at 0.25% and redeemed in 3 months pays the 5% floor of $50; a 0% bid gets no minimum at all.

text.title: A $1,000 lien bid at 0.25% and redeemed in 3 months pays the 5% floor of $50; a 0% bid gets no minimum at all.

rect.title: step: 05; label: Log Dates and Reserve Legal Fees; value: Step 5; detail: Record redemption and expiration dates the day you buy (Florida certificates expire without a deed application within seven years) and reserve roughly $2,000 to $5,000 per file for attorney and foreclosure fees.

text.title: Log Dates and Reserve Legal Fees

Record redemption and expiration dates the day you buy (Florida certificates expire without a deed application within seven years) and reserve roughly $2,000 to $5,000 per file for attorney and foreclosure fees.
Assumptions: Rates and redemption floors are state-specific practitioner claims; the five-step order is an organizing sequence built from their separate tips.
